rationale: Captured-call dtype ablations isolate a NaN-producing routing tie at a sharp context threshold.
title: [Bug] GLM-5.2-NVFP4 + flashinfer_trtllm: long-context outputs collapse to '!!!!' (NaN logits) — fp32 correction_bias regression from #29783
optimization: ModelOpt FP4 with flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner; FP8 KV cache
runtime_hardware: SGLang v0.5.15 or a build containing d8462f49619; 4× NVIDIA B300 / SM103, TP=4; standalone failing-kernel replay on 1 GPU
observed_failure: Beyond roughly 6.5k tokens for triggering content, output becomes repeated '!' characters; requested token logprobs are null because logits become all-NaN. Short requests are reported as healthy.
baseline_or_control: FP8 checkpoints of the same model are unaffected. Captured-call ablations report fp32 routing bias produces NaNs, while casting the same values to bf16, adding 10 to logits, or de-duplicating the bias produces clean output. A pre-regression build was healthy, and half-revert bisection identified d8462f49619.
mechanism: Removal of the bf16 correction-bias branch leaves an fp32 routing bias on the FP4 path. For very negative router logits, sigmoid contributions vanish at the fp32 bias scale; duplicated bias values then create exact ties across the top-8 boundary, and flashinfer routingCustom emits NaN expert weights that propagate to all logits. Standalone replay also shows the kernel's underlying defect is NaN-producing tie handling, not dtype alone.
discriminating_test: Replay the captured routing call with identical logits and weights, changing only routing_bias from fp32 to bf16; NaN only with fp32 localizes the failure to runtime routing rather than FP4 expert-weight damage.
missing_information: Whether closure corresponds to a merged fix | Fix commit or released version | resolution
